lastText: File ClosedThe Ring, Closed After the FactMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1941–1945End of hostilities: JANUARY 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around January 1945: earlier than the historical May 1945, bought with a faster, costlier advance. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over: a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The drive on Rostov closed the door on Army Group A: the encirclement history reached for and missed, landed on this path at the favorable edge of what the winter logistics allowed. The Izyum salient was given up before the Germans could close it. The armies, tanks and guns the real offensive lost in May 1942 went into the summer instead, and Case Blue met a southern front that had them. The autumn 1942 reserve was weighted entirely south: Mars never launched, the Rzhev grinder's cost declined, and the single-theater concentration tested against the pinning argument Mars's defenders always made. Berlin's fall was a certainty from the day the front stopped moving west; everything this campaign tracked was the cost of the miles back.One Year LaterVictory arrived ahead of the historical May 1945, which means the occupation of eastern and central Europe has had that much longer to harden by the time this account picks back up a year later.
